one_liner: Rust UI framework whose web renderer runs a WebAssembly virtual DOM; about 1.43x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark.
what_it_does: Dioxus is a Rust framework for web, desktop, mobile and server-rendered apps. Components are Rust functions that return `rsx!` markup and hold state in signals (`use_signal`). The web renderer (dioxus-web) compiles the app to wasm32 and drives the browser DOM, launched with `dioxus_web::launch::launch(app, ...)` or through the `dx` CLI. It is a different language and API from React (Rust plus rsx!, not JSX), so it is not a drop-in replacement.
how_it_is_fast: rsx! splits markup into static templates and dynamic slots at compile time. dioxus-core diffs only the dynamic parts, and the JS side clones a saved template with `cloneNode(true)` instead of rebuilding it element by element. DOM edits are not one wasm-bindgen call each: dioxus-interpreter-js (sledgehammer_bindgen) writes them as op codes into u8/u16/u32 buffers in wasm memory, decodes strings once per batch with a TextDecoder, caches attribute and namespace names, and replays the whole batch in one `run()` call after each `render_immediate`. Signals re-render only the components that read them, so the keyed swap row does not re-render the list. That row is where React hooks is slow: 14.6 vs 89.7 ms.
when_to_use: Rust teams that want one component codebase for web, desktop (webview), mobile and SSR, and still want keyed-list DOM performance at or above React 19 hooks.
Large keyed tables or lists that are reordered, partly updated or selected often (swap 6.1x, select 1.9x and create 10,000 rows 1.55x faster than React hooks in the suite, derived from page data).
Apps whose domain logic is already in Rust, which can share types with an axum backend through Dioxus server functions instead of a JSON layer.
Interactive single-page apps where per-interaction latency matters more than first load.
when_not_to_use: First-load-sensitive pages: in the same run the bundle is 114.9 kB brotli vs React's 51.4 kB, and first paint is 540.9 vs 226.6 ms. The README's '50kb hello world' is not this app's size.

When you need the fastest DOM framework: Dioxus takes 1.27x the time of vanillajs-keyed, 1.15x Solid, 1.07x Svelte and 1.20x the hand-written wasm-bindgen entry, and ties Vue 3.5 (derived from page data). Clearing rows is its weakest benchmark (16.6 vs 8.7 ms for vanilla). The removeAllChildren fast path, issue #573, has been open since 2022.

Memory-constrained or long-lived pages with heavy row churn: memory after 5 create/clear cycles is 6.74 MB, against 1.98 MB for React hooks, 4.59 MB for Leptos and 3.55 MB for Sycamore. The figure is higher than after a single 1k run (6.12 MB).
Sites that enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy: the suite flags the implementation with note 1139 (fails `default-src 'self'`).

SSR-heavy or Safari-heavy workloads: issue #4216 (open) says dioxus-ssr performs worse than other templating engines. #3076 reported 20-30 s updates in Safari 17.6 on a page of about 2,000 items; it was closed without a fix being named, and maintainers attributed it to Safari's style recalculation.

integration.dependencies: dioxus-core, dioxus-html, dioxus-signals, dioxus-web, dioxus-interpreter-js (sledgehammer_bindgen, sledgehammer_utils), wasm-bindgen, js-sys, web-sys; build with the dx CLI or trunk for wasm32-unknown-unknown
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.80 (rust-version of the dioxus 0.7.2 crate); main is edition 2024 with 0.8.0-alpha.1. The benchmark binary was built with rustc 1.92.0 and wasm-bindgen 0.2.106 (read from the shipped wasm).
integration.platforms: Any browser with WebAssembly for the web renderer. Other renderers cover desktop and mobile (webview), SSR and liveview, plus an experimental WGPU native renderer.
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the files read; the web renderer runs one VirtualDom event loop on the browser main thread

gotchas: Harness flaw, load-time only: the benchmark loads frameworks/keyed/dioxus/bundled-dist/index.html (customURL since 2026-01-24), which is hand-edited. An added inline module script starts dioxus_benchmark.js. Trunk-generated preload tags and a second `await init(...)` script are left in, and they point to server-root files (/dioxus_benchmark-32c73e936749f4d4.js, its _bg.wasm, /snippets/...) that are not in the repository. Those requests fail at page load, which can touch the first-paint and size rows but not the nine CPU rows. The top-level index.html points at a third build (dioxus_benchmark-1e3bca78-...) whose files are also missing.

Toolchain behind the prebuilt bundle, recovered from the shipped wasm: strings for dioxus-core, dioxus-web and dioxus-signals 0.7.2, a producers section with wasm-bindgen 0.2.106 (11831fb89) and walrus 0.24.4, and rustc commit ded5c06cf ('[stable] prepare Rust 1.92.0'). So the binary matches the declared 0.7.2 source (commit 5ac9bd0, 2026-01-14). There is no Cargo.lock, and `build-prod` is a no-op.

Dioxus core developers tuned the suite implementation (jkelleyrtp 2022; ealmloff 2024, 'optimize the dioxus implementation and don't leak memory'). It uses a `Signal<String>` per row updated with `write_unchecked`, a `use_set_compare` selector for the selected row, and `use_drop` + `manually_drop` for row signals. Signals created with `Signal::new` in an event handler belong to the enclosing scope and leak in long lists unless dropped like this.
Benchmarked version is 0.7.2 (December 2025); crates.io has 0.7.10 (2026-07-30) and 0.8.0-alpha.1, and the suite has not re-measured them.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against the other Rust/Wasm siblings, the CPU rows are a tie: Dioxus takes 1.02x Leptos's time, 0.98x Sycamore's and 1.03x rust-dominator's, all derived from page data. Leptos and Sycamore ship well under half the bundle (48.8 and 47.2 kB vs 114.9 kB compressed) and use less memory. Pick Dioxus for its desktop and mobile renderers, hot-patching dx tooling and fullstack server functions, not for raw DOM speed or size.
verified_claims_summary: In krausest/js-framework-benchmark's Chrome 154.0.8037.98 development snapshot (MacBook Pro 14, Apple M4, macOS 26.6.2), the keyed Dioxus 0.7.2 build took 0.698x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed. That figure is the unweighted geometric mean of the nine median total durations, and I reproduced it from results.ts. The gain is mostly swap rows (14.6 vs 89.7 ms) and create 10,000 rows (257.9 vs 401.0 ms); without swap it is 0.838x, and create 1,000 rows is 2% slower. The same data puts it level with Vue 3.5 (1.002x) and behind vanillajs (1.272x), Solid (1.151x) and Svelte 5 (1.073x).
status_note: Active and copyable: 39.4k stars, MIT OR Apache-2.0, dioxus-web 0.7.10 released 2026-07-30 and 0.8.0-alpha.1 on main, 661 open issues. The suite numbers are for 0.7.2, eight patch releases old, measured on a development snapshot; the bundle's build is load-time-sloppy but traceable to the declared source.
